Name: leave_one_type_out_split
Title: Within-Type Splits Inflate Transfer: A Leave-One-Type-Out Composite Shows Retrieval Gains Are Type-Bound, Harm Tracks Within-Type Gain, and Only Weights Carry Portable Competence
Short Hypothesis: The standard ALFWorld splits (valid_seen/valid_unseen) always leave same-type items in the bank, so every measured transfer gain is procedure retrieval. Under a leave-one-type-out (LOTO) composite, in which each of the 274 validation games is read against a bank lacking its own task type, retrieval gains from every writer collapse below +8 net, and the writer that helps most within-type (the off-policy expert, whose items the reader follows most closely) becomes harmful under type shift while the reader's own pool stays near neutral. The harm is a following behaviour, not a knowledge deficit, so it survives even when the missing competence is put into the weights. Absorbing the same expert pool into QLoRA adapters, evaluated with the matching LOTO adapter, retains a positive type-portable gain (navigation and action validity) net of a five-procedure static prompt, so the retrieval-versus-weights ranking flips between splits at matched cost.
Related Work: PAST-Bench (arxiv:2608.04003) toggles retained experience and S3Gym (arxiv:2608.31100) compares history ICL, summaries and training, but neither holds out a task type or swaps the writer. AgentCL (arxiv:2606.02461) builds controlled task streams for continual learning without cross-writer or held-out-type transfer. Retrieval-aware fine-tuning (arxiv:2603.18272) claims generalization to unseen tasks but does not compare retrieval and weights under the same held-out split with writer identity manipulated. Parametric memories (PEAM arxiv:2605.27762; fast-weight memory arxiv:2606.04536) assert efficiency and portability on one environment and backbone (digest gap G25). MemHarness (arxiv:2607.28272) shows verbatim replay of retrieved experience causes negative transfer out of distribution, on self-written experience and without a weights arm, so it cannot say whether the harm persists once the competence is in the weights. In the home literature, in-context learning with mismatched demonstrations is known to hurt or help depending on evidence mixture (arxiv:2605.26350) and cross-task demonstration transfer can help (CrossICL arxiv:2505.24143), but no work couples the harm of wrong-task demonstrations to how strongly the same demonstrations help in-task, across demonstrators. Measurement A on this node found unseen ~ seen with the full bank (a room split, not a type split) and Measurement B provides the QLoRA arm. Archived context_wins_substrate_conflict (5.55) concerned substrate conflict within-type; here the split, not the conflict, is the manipulated variable.
Abstract: Transfer of agent experience is evaluated on splits that keep same-type experience in the bank, so the gain reported is the gain of finding a same-type procedure. We propose a leave-one-type-out (LOTO) composite for ALFWorld: six banks each missing one task type, and every one of the 274 validation games read against the bank that lacks its type, giving one full-size cell per writer x reader instead of six under-powered per-type cells. Writer identity is manipulated (expert walkthroughs; Qwen3-32B's own successes; EXAONE-4.0-32B's own successes at the same collection budget) with one retriever and one item format; readers are Qwen3-32B and EXAONE-4.0-32B. The same expert pool is absorbed into QLoRA rank-32 adapters (one all-type adapter as in Measurement B and six LOTO adapters), served by vLLM multi-LoRA so the adapter composite runs as one cell; adapters are evaluated memory-absent, matched (their own pool) and mismatched (the self pool). Controls: k=0, six- and five-procedure static prompts (the LOTO analog of Measurement C), a random-other-type token-matched placebo, and a wrong-procedure graft at 100% as the Gate-0 positive control. The cells that carry the claims run at 8 seeds (MDE +/-4 net) and every prediction has one pre-registered decision boundary with the hypothesis and its named rival each at least one MDE from it. Predictions: LOTO retrieval gain below +8 for every writer whose within-type gain is at least +16 (headline: the expert pool in the Qwen3 reader, predicted -8); the expert pool at least 6 net worse than the self pool under LOTO and at least 4 net below k=0; the LOTO adapter at least +6 over the five-procedure prompt and at least +12 over LOTO retrieval of the same pool, while within-type retrieval beats the all-type adapter by at least +8; and the expert items still cost at least 4 net when retrieved on top of the matching LOTO adapter, so the harm is a following behaviour rather than a knowledge deficit. Estimands: within-type gain, LOTO gain, their paired difference (the type-bound fraction), the retained-gain ratio per writer x reader under each split, and cost per net point for weights versus retrieval. About 28,300 episodes plus 17 GPU-hours of collection and training, two days on two A100s.
Experiments: Preparation (about half a day): render pools by env replay; construct six LOTO banks per writer keyed on the ALFWorld task-type label (pick-two and pick-and-place recorded as a skeleton-similar pair; a seventh bank excludes both); build the wrong-procedure graft pool (each item's appliance step swapped to the wrong appliance, replay-checked to fail); build the five-procedure static prompt per target type (target type's procedure omitted, token-matched to k=3). Collection on GPU1: EXAONE-4.0-32B k=0 pool on the train split at the same episode budget as the existing Qwen3-32B self pool (about 3 GPU-hours). Training on GPU1 while GPU0 serves: seven QLoRA r32 adapters on the expert pool (six LOTO adapters first, then the all-type adapter as in Measurement B; about 2 GPU-hours each, 14 GPU-hours), served through vLLM multi-LoRA on the bf16 base with per-request adapter selection so each adapter composite is one cell. Reader cells, all 274 validation games, episodes = 274 x seeds. Qwen3-32B reader, k=3 unless noted: [1] k=0, 8 seeds, 2,192; [2] five-procedure static prompt, 8 seeds, 2,192; [3] LOTO expert, 8 seeds, 2,192; [4] LOTO self, 8 seeds, 2,192; [5] LOTO EXAONE-writer, 4 seeds, 1,096; [6] standard expert (Measurement A's 2 seeds plus 2 new), 548 new; [7] standard self, 4 seeds, 1,096; [8] standard EXAONE-writer, 2 seeds, 548; [9] random-other-type placebo, 2 seeds, 548; [10] wrong-procedure graft at 100%, 4 seeds, 1,096 (Gate 0); [11] joint-exclusion bank (pick-two and pick-and-place removed together), expert writer, on the roughly 90 games of those two types, 4 seeds, about 360; [12] LOTO adapter composite, memory-absent, 8 seeds, 2,192; [13] all-type adapter, memory-absent, 4 seeds, 1,096; [14] LOTO adapter + LOTO expert retrieval (matched), 8 seeds, 2,192; [15] all-type adapter + standard expert retrieval (matched), 2 seeds, 548; [16] LOTO adapter + LOTO self retrieval (mismatched), 4 seeds, 1,096. Qwen3 subtotal about 21,200 episodes. EXAONE-4.0-32B reader (4-seed replication): [17] k=0, 4 seeds, 1,096; [18] five-procedure static, 4 seeds, 1,096; [19] six-procedure static (Measurement C analog), 2 seeds, 548; [20] LOTO expert, 4 seeds, 1,096; [21] LOTO own, 4 seeds, 1,096; [22] LOTO Qwen3-writer, 2 seeds, 548; [23-25] standard expert, own, Qwen3-writer, 2 seeds each, 1,644. EXAONE subtotal about 7,100. Total about 28,300 episodes; at the sibling measurements' rate of about 1,100 episodes per replica-hour at saturating concurrency, about 26 replica-hours. Schedule: hours 0-13 GPU0 serves the Qwen3 base reader (cells 1-11, about 14,100 episodes) while GPU1 collects (3 h) then trains (14 h); the roughly 2-hour gap before the six LOTO adapters land at hour 15 is filled by the optional k=1 ablation cells; hours 15-21.5 GPU0 runs the adapter cells (12, 14, 16, then 13 and 15 once the all-type adapter lands at hour 17; about 7,100 episodes); hours 17-23.5 GPU1 serves the EXAONE reader (about 7,100 episodes). About 24 serving wall-hours plus preparation: about 2 days, both GPUs busy throughout. Per cell: success, net vs k=0 and vs the appropriate static prompt, per type, seen/unseen, injected tokens, steps, retained-gain ratio, and cost per net point (collection GPU-hours, training GPU-hours, consumer tokens).
Baselines and Ablations: k=0 (8 seeds in the Qwen3 reader, the shared reference); six-procedure static prompt (Measurement C) for standard cells and five-procedure static prompt (target type omitted, token-matched to k=3; 8 seeds) for LOTO cells; self-pool control at matched collection cost (Qwen3 and EXAONE k=0 successes on the train split at the same episode budget), read under both splits; random-other-type token-matched placebo to separate nearest-wrong-type retrieval from any wrong-type content; wrong-procedure graft at 100% as the Gate-0 positive control (harm of at least 6 net required, 4 seeds), which is also the manufactured contamination arm at a controlled rate by writer identity (the LOTO bank itself is a 100% wrong-type arm per writer; no read-time detector is claimed); adapters evaluated memory-absent, matched (LOTO adapter + LOTO expert retrieval; all-type adapter + standard expert retrieval) and mismatched (LOTO adapter + LOTO self retrieval), the adaptation step compared with direct injection of the same unmodified items at k=3; joint-exclusion bank (pick-two and pick-and-place removed together) on those two types' games as the leakage check; the EXAONE reader as a 4-seed replication of every headline contrast; retained-gain ratio per writer x reader under each split. If time permits after the listed cells: k=1 LOTO cells for expert and self (retrieval-strength ablation, 2 seeds each) and one all-type adapter trained on the self pool (2 GPU-hours) as the writer ablation for the parametric arm. The writer set spans proximity at roughly matched capability (Qwen3-32B vs EXAONE-4.0-32B) and capability at low proximity (expert walkthroughs), but the manipulated variable of this design is the split, not proximity.
Falsifiable Predictions: Noise budget (from the brief): a paired net between two cells at 274 games x 2 seeds has CI half-width +/-8; the half-width scales as 1/sqrt(seeds/2), so +/-5.7 at 4 seeds and +/-4 at 8 seeds; a contrast between two non-reference cells is charged the larger half-width of the pair. Every clause has one pre-registered decision boundary, decided by the point estimate with the CI reported, and the value predicted by the hypothesis and by its named rival each lie at least one MDE from the boundary. P1 (headline, type-bound retrieval). P1a: in the Qwen3 reader, the expert pool's LOTO gain (cell 3 minus cell 1, 8 seeds each, MDE +/-4) is below +8 net while its standard-bank gain (cell 6 minus cell 1) is at least +16 (Measurement A gives about +27). The hypothesis predicts LOTO about -8 (2 MDE below the boundary); the rival, that expert items carry portable navigation and action-validity knowledge, predicts at least +16 (half the within-type gain, 2 MDE above). Falsifier: cell 3 minus cell 1 at or above +8. P1b: the same +8 bound holds for every other writer x reader LOTO cell (cells 4, 5, 20, 21, 22; MDE +/-4 to +/-8) whose standard-bank gain is at least +16; a writer that fails the +16 premise is reported, not counted. Falsifier: any qualifying LOTO cell at or above +8. Arm: LOTO banks for three writers x two readers. P2 (harm tracks within-type gain; gated on Gate 0). P2a (premise, within-type): expert standard gain exceeds self standard gain by at least +6 in the Qwen3 reader (cell 6 minus cell 7, 4 seeds each, MDE +/-5.7; predicted +9; the proximity rival of closer_beats_stronger predicts at most 0). Falsifier: below +6. P2b (coupling): under LOTO the expert pool is worse than the self pool by at least 6 net (cell 3 minus cell 4, 8 seeds each, MDE +/-4; predicted -10, expert -8 and self +2; the rival that wrong-type harm is writer-independent, or that self items harm as much, predicts 0). Falsifier: cell 3 minus cell 4 above -6. P2c (sign): expert LOTO net vs k=0 is at most -4 (cell 3 minus cell 1, MDE +/-4; predicted -8 or worse, the graft control giving the ceiling; the rival that wrong-type expert items are ignored predicts 0). Falsifier: above -4. The EXAONE reader (cells 20, 21, 17; MDE +/-5.7) replicates P2b and P2c at the same boundaries. Gate 0: the wrong-procedure graft (cell 10, 4 seeds, MDE +/-5.7) must show harm of at least 6 net vs k=0 (predicted -15 or worse); if it does not, the reader is insensitive to wrong items and P2 and P4 are void, not confirmed. P3 (substrate flip). P3a: the LOTO adapter composite, memory-absent, beats the five-procedure static prompt by at least +6 net (cell 12 minus cell 2, 8 seeds each, MDE +/-4; predicted +10, adapter +12 and static-5 +2; the rival that the adapter overfits the trained types, or that five procedures carry the same generic gain, predicts at most 0). Falsifier: below +6. P3b: under LOTO, weights beat retrieval of the same expert pool by at least +12 (cell 12 minus cell 3, MDE +/-4; predicted +20; rival at most +4). Falsifier: below +12; P1a and P3a together bound this difference only from below near 0, so the +12 boundary is a separate claim. P3c: within-type, retrieval beats weights by at least +8 (cell 6 minus cell 13, 4 seeds each, MDE +/-5.7; predicted +15; the rival that weights match retrieval within-type predicts at most 0). Falsifier: below +8. Arm: adapter cells vs retrieval cells on the same games. P4 (harm survives weights): adding LOTO retrieval of the expert pool on top of the matching LOTO adapter lowers success by at least 4 net relative to the adapter alone (cell 14 minus cell 12, 8 seeds each, MDE +/-4; predicted -8, because the reader still follows the wrong-type procedure; the rival that weights make the reader robust to wrong items, or that it now ignores them, predicts 0 or better). Falsifier: cell 14 minus cell 12 above -4. Arm: matched adapter-plus-retrieval cell vs memory-absent adapter cell. The seen/unseen decomposition of every cell is reported descriptively with its contrast MDE (+/-8 at 8 seeds) and carries no prediction. Shared cells: P1a, P2c and P3b read the same LOTO expert cell, and P3a, P3b and P4 the same LOTO adapter cell; each clause has its own rival outcome that the shared cell can show, and the boundaries are set so no clause follows from the others. None is entailed: other-type items could teach navigation (P1), self items could harm as much as expert items or proximity could beat the expert within-type (P2), adapters could overfit to the trained types or match retrieval within-type (P3), and weights could make the reader ignore wrong items (P4).
Measurement and Noise Control: All cells are paired on the same 274 games, seeds and retrieval ordering; game-level stratified bootstrap CIs. Noise budget from the brief: +/-8 net for a paired net at 274 x 2 seeds, scaling as 1/sqrt(seeds/2) (+/-5.7 at 4, +/-4 at 8); a contrast between two non-reference cells is charged the larger half-width of the pair. The scaling is verified on the first two 8-seed cells (k=0 and static-5) by computing the half-width at 2, 4 and 8 seeds before any LOTO cell runs; if the 8-seed half-width exceeds +/-5, the boundaries stay and each clause is reported against its measured MDE. One decision boundary per clause, decided by the point estimate with the CI reported; no confirm/falsify dead zone. Margins as fractions of the Gate-0 effect (6 net): 4 (two-thirds), 6 (one), 8 (four-thirds), 12 (two). The type-bound fraction is the paired difference (standard minus LOTO on the same games) with its CI; the retained-gain ratio (reader's gain from the writer's pool over the writer's own gain from it, or over the reader's self-pool gain) is reported with a bootstrap CI under the standard split and as a paired difference under LOTO, where denominators are near zero. The seen/unseen decomposition is descriptive (contrast MDE +/-8 at 8 seeds). Adapter cost is charged in GPU-hours per reader and retrieval cost in injected tokens per episode, both converted to cost per net point under each split. Order: k=0, static prompts and the graft positive control first (Gate 0 must pass before any harm claim), then LOTO retrieval cells, standard cells, then adapter cells as adapters land; adapter training and EXAONE collection run on GPU1 throughout so no replica idles. Queue occupancy (running/waiting) and episodes per replica-hour are logged per cell, and concurrency is raised until the serving queue saturates.

Risk Factors and Limitations: vLLM multi-LoRA applies rank-32 deltas to the bf16 base rather than the 4-bit base used in QLoRA training; the all-type adapter's within-type result is checked against Measurement B's evaluation path, with merge-and-serve-sequentially (six extra replica launches) as the fallback. The throughput assumption (about 1,100 episodes per replica-hour) comes from the sibling measurements; if it is lower, seeds are cut first on the ablation cells (placebo, joint exclusion, all-type matched, mismatched, the EXAONE 2-seed cells) and never on the six 8-seed cells that carry P1-P4. If the second backbone is unavailable the EXAONE cells drop and the writer set shrinks to expert and self, which still decides P1a, P2, P3 and P4 but reduces P1b to two cells and removes the replication. Type exclusion by label may leak through skeleton-similar types, hence the joint-exclusion bank. P2a may fail (self at or above expert within-type), which falsifies the premise that the expert is the most-followed writer; the coupling would then be re-read on the measured top writer and labelled post hoc. LOTO harm may be above the boundary for all writers (a null on P2 and P4) while P1 and P3 stay informative. Eight-seed cells assume seed-to-seed variance is a substantial part of the paired noise; the scaling check on the first two cells guards this, and if it fails the affected clauses are reported at their measured MDE rather than re-thresholded. ALFWorld's six types are few; the composite generalizes to any typed task set but the specific numbers do not.
Addresses gap: G23 (primary: the same artifacts read by different readers under a split that removes same-type coverage, with the retained fraction per writer x reader); G25 for the adapter arm (parametric portability across a held-out split at matched cost, and whether weights remove the harm of wrong-type retrieval).
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet: 'unseen ~ seen (procedure-bound)' in Measurement A is a room split with same-type items always present; this idea holds out the type itself, predicts the collapse and sign reversal of retrieval gains, and couples the harm to within-type gain across writers. Digest card arxiv:2608.04003 (PAST-Bench) toggles retained experience on and off for one writer and reader; this idea toggles which type the bank covers, swaps the writer, and adds the parametric pathway under the same split. Archived context_wins_substrate_conflict (5.55) claimed context beats weights when substrates conflict, within-type; this idea claims the evaluation split, not the conflict, decides the ranking, with retrieval winning within-type and weights winning under type shift, and it is the first to run Measurement B's adapter under a held-out-type composite. MemHarness (arxiv:2607.28272) shows negative transfer from self-written experience under shift with no weights arm; P4 asks whether that harm persists once the competence is in the weights.
Changes made: P1: headline moved from the valid_unseen half (about 134 games, +/-11) to the full 274-game composite; the cells that carry it (k=0, static-5, LOTO expert, LOTO self, LOTO adapter, matched adapter+retrieval) raised to 8 seeds (MDE +/-4); one decision boundary (+8) with the hypothesis (-8) and the rival (+16) each 2 MDE from it; the +16 within-type premise kept; split into P1a (expert, Qwen3 reader) and P1b (every other writer x reader). P2: exact Kendall tau=1 over three writers replaced by a pre-registered expert-versus-self contrast under LOTO with a 6-net boundary at 8 seeds, plus an explicit within-type premise clause (expert over self by 6) that the proximity rival can falsify; the absolute harm boundary set at -4 (one MDE below zero, two-thirds of Gate 0) with the graft as the ceiling; the EXAONE reader made a 4-seed replication. P3: three clauses each with one boundary; the LOTO adapter is now scored net of the five-procedure static prompt (absorbing the old P4 and its 4-to-6 dead zone); the LOTO weights-over-retrieval boundary raised to +12 so it is not supplied by P1a and P3a. Old P4 (static-prompt survival) merged into P3a. New P4 added: harm survives weights (matched LOTO adapter + LOTO expert retrieval vs the adapter alone, 8 seeds, boundary -4), which sharpens the harm mechanism to following rather than ignorance and uses the mandated matched arm to carry a claim. P5 removed: the seen-minus-unseen contrast has MDE +/-8 even at 8 seeds and no arm at this budget resolves a 10-net half-cell contrast; the decomposition is reported descriptively and the 4-seed special cell is dropped. Budget: about 28,300 episodes (from 12,100), 26 replica-hours plus 17 GPU-hours of collection and training overlapped on GPU1, still about 2 days; k=1 ablation and the self-pool adapter moved to 'if time permits'; a seed-scaling check on the first two 8-seed cells added. Sharpness kept: the central claims (collapse below +8, sign reversal for the expert pool, flip of the substrate ranking) are unchanged in magnitude; the objections were answered by adding seeds to the cells that carry the claims and by extending the harm claim to the weights arm, not by hedging it.
